messages.author: 0ee8ae7c0d185529
messages.subject: chi="all" in sem.mi
parts:
Dear all, 

When running the following lines

fitmi <- sem.mi(pathmodel,scimodel,m=5,miPackage="mice",chi="all")
summary(fitmi,fit.measures=TRUE)
inspect(fitmi, what="fit")

I don't receive all of the chi-squares based on different poolings.  The semTools package states

chi

   The method to combine the chi-square. Can be one of the following: "mr" for the method proposed for Meng & Rubin (1992), "mplus" for the method used in Mplus (Asparouhov & Muthen, 2010), "lmrr" for the method proposed by Li, Meng, Raghunathan, & Rubin (1991), "all" to show the three methods in the output, and"none" to not pool any chi-square values. The default is "all"


What am I missing?


Thanks


David

messages.author: af82fa98896529e2
messages.subject: Re: chi="all" in sem.mi
parts:
Hi David,

Could you try the following script?

inspect(pathmodel, "impute")

If all variables are continuous, the chi-square values of all three methods should be available. If any variables are categorical, only Li et al's (2011) approach is used. We are not sure how to use the Meng and Rubin's (2012) method and Mplus modification for categorical cases because the likelihood values are not available in weighted least square estimator. If anyone in the list have any suggestions, please let me know.

Best,
Sunthud

messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: chi="all" in sem.mi
parts:
Sunthud beat me to the reply. You could also use the following code to only access fit information:

inspect(fitmi, what="impute")$targetFit #for the fit of the target model
inspect(fitmi, what="impute")$nullFit #for the fit of the null model

To convert the F statistics from the lmrr and mr methods to chi square statistics, simply multiply the F value by df1 (note that the mr chi square and mplus chi square will be identical).

Alex

messages.author: af82fa98896529e2
messages.subject: Re: chi="all" in sem.mi
parts:
The LMRR and MR approaches provide the F values but the Mplus approach provide the chi-square value. Mplus uses the asymptotic property of the F distribution such that, if the denominator df is large, the F distribution multiplied by the numerator df is convergent to the chi-square distribution with the df equal to the numerator df of the F distribution. You will see that the F value of the MR approach multiplied by 10 (degree of freedom) is the Mplus chi-square value.

Sunthud
